title: gaze-relevance: perceived text relevance from eye movements on short and long documents
description: Code accompanying the article 'A Comparative Analysis of Gaze-Based Representations for Perceived Text Relevance Estimation Across Short and Long Documents' (Scientific Reports). A fully documented Jupyter notebook downloads the public gazeRE eye-tracking dataset and reproduces all feature-based results: extraction of the 17 gaze features with the official gazeRE code, participant fold assignments, nested algorithm selection, the 3-second visit filter, participant-disjoint transfer from short (g-REL) to long (GoogleNQ) documents with per-reader normalisation, feature analyses (permutation importance, SHAP, PCA), generalisation to unseen documents, and corrected statistical tests. A separate script reproduces the VTNet and VGG19 analyses on a GPU. The code builds on the gazeRE dataset repository (data loader, feature extraction) and the GNN-Scanpath-Analysis-ICMI2024 repository (generation of the image representations); the eye-tracking data are not redistributed and are downloaded from the gazeRE repository.
